sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Poverty Line Definition**: The threshold income or consumption expenditure required to satisfy a minimum acceptable standard of living, historically anchored in **calorie intake norms** and later expanded to **multidimensional and monthly per capita consumption expenditure (MPCE)**.
• **Absolute vs Relative Poverty**: **Absolute poverty** measures headcount ratio against a fixed absolute poverty line; **relative poverty** measures inequality across income deciles or quintiles.
• **Employment Metrics**: Measured through **Usual Principal Status (UPS)**, **Usual Principal and Subsidiary Status (UPSS)**, and **Current Daily Status (CDS)** via periodic labour force surveys.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Transition from single-dimensional calorie intake to multi-dimensional indicators encompassing health, education, and standard of living.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: VM Dandekar & N Rath (1971)
First systematic assessment based on nutritional requirement of 2250 calories per capita per day for rural and urban areas.
Single uniform calorie norm; focused on inadequacy of actual consumption.
Foundational baseline for subsequent academic and official poverty debates.
Y.K. Alagh Committee (1979)
Task Force constituted by Planning Commission; defined poverty line based on nutritional requirements (2100 calories for urban, 2400 calories for rural).
State-specific poverty lines using rural-urban calorie differentiation.
First official adoption of calorie-based poverty lines by the Planning Commission.
Lakdawala Committee (1993)
Expert Group; retained Alagh calorie norms but scaled them using CPI-CL (Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers) and CPI-IW.
State-specific lines; assumed consumption basket remains fixed over time.
Widely used by Planning Commission for official poverty estimates for decades.
Suresh Tendulkar Committee (2009)
Moved away from pure calorie intake; included health and education expenditure; used Mixed Reference Period (MRP).
All-India urban poverty line used as anchor; derived rural poverty line based on basket differences.
Abandoned calorie fetishism; significantly raised poverty headcount ratios (around 37.2% in 2004-05).
C. Rangarajan Committee (2014)
Constituted to review Tendulkar methodology; recommended higher poverty lines (rural MPCE Rs. 972, urban MPCE Rs. 1407 per month).
Used normative levels of nourishment plus non-food expenses (clothing, education, health, housing).
Estimated poverty at 29.5% (2011-12); acknowledged higher poverty levels than Tendulkar.

items.definition: Consumption data collected for a 30-day recall period for all items (food and non-food) used by early committees like Lakdawala.
Consumption data collected with a 365-day recall period for infrequent items (clothing, footwear, education, institutional health) and 30-day recall for remaining items (Tendulkar methodology).

Recall period of 7 days for edible oil, eggs, fish, meat, vegetables, fruits, spices, beverages, etc.; 30 days for apparel, footwear, education, institutional medical care; 365 days for remaining non-food items (NITI Aayog task force baseline).
Committee on Unemployment (Bhagwati) assessed nature and extent of unemployment; Dantwala Committee evaluated estimates of unemployment by the NSSO.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Inter-State Disparities**: Higher poverty concentrations traditionally observed in central and eastern states (Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh).
• **Urban-Rural Divide**: Shift of poverty dynamics due to distress migration, urban informal sector expansion, and agrarian stagnation.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Lack of consensus on a single definitive poverty line; exclusion errors in targeted welfare schemes.
• **Policy Interventions**: Shift towards NITI Aayog's Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) based on NFHS data; JAM Trinity (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) for leakage-proof transfers.

items.title: Mnemonic for Poverty Committee Chronology
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "**A**ll **L**abours **T**ry **R**ight"
• **Decoded Meaning**: **A**lagh (1979) -> **L**akdawala (1993) -> **T**endulkar (2009) -> **R**angarajan (2014).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly solves chronological arrangement questions in Prelims.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Calorie focus ended with Tendulkar; Multidimensional metrics started post-Tendulkar leading to NITI Aayog's MPI.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states that the Tendulkar or Rangarajan Committee recommendations were officially accepted and implemented by the government as the operational poverty line. Note that while Tendulkar estimates were used, Rangarajan report was submitted to the Planning Commission (later NITI Aayog) but no official consensus or adoption as the sole poverty line has been finalized yet.

Mains Value Addition: In GS-3 answers, emphasize that poverty is no longer viewed purely through consumption expenditure, but through the lens of NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) measuring health, education, and standard of living across 12 indicators.

keyTakeaways: Poverty estimation evolved from purely nutritional calorie metrics (Alagh, Lakdawala) to broader consumption baskets (Tendulkar, Rangarajan).
Employment committees like Bhagwati and Dantwala laid the groundwork for robust labor force measurement via NSSO/PLFS surveys.
Modern policy has transitioned from monetary poverty lines to Multidimensional Poverty Indices (MPI).
